roadmap.goal: Deliverable A (v0.19.0): an instance admin turns on Matrix and Slack at /admin/instance/integrations (Generate the secrets key wrapped by the instance key from FOUNDRY_INSTANCE_KEY, the legacy FOUNDRY_SECRETS_KEY, or a Foundry-made key file; Move legacy direct seals under it; save the Foundry Slack app), live on every replica without a restart (US-IIS-01, 02, 03, 06, 08).
roadmap.scenario_ownership_invariant: 41 scenario declarations (59 examples) in instance-integration-setup.feature, each owned by exactly one step, no orphans: 01-01 1 (2), 02-01 3 (3), 02-02 4 (4), 02-03 3 (11), 02-04 2 (2), 03-01 3 (3), 03-02 1 (6), 03-03 6 (6), 03-04 2 (2), 04-01 4 (5), 05-01 4 (7), 05-02 4 (4), 05-03 1 (1), 06-01 3 (3). Totals 41 declarations, 59 examples. Steps 01-02, 01-03 and 06-03 own none (infrastructure). 06-02 owns the one new DEVOPS-assigned scenario outside this file, 'The image gives Foundry a private data directory it keeps as a volume' (@docker-compose, us-01-install.feature), and the amended shipped scenario us-01 @nfr-port-01. Grand total owned: 41 IIS declarations + 1 new image-shape scenario = 42 declarations (60 examples), plus 1 changed shipped scenario.
regression_guards: @external-integration-plugins suite, unchanged (KPI-IIS-G3): legacy FOUNDRY_SECRETS_KEY seals keep opening, partial SLACK_* trio and FOUNDRY_SECRETS_KEY_PREVIOUS behave as shipped
@integrations-wayfinding suite, unchanged (KPI-IIS-G3): W-2/W-3/K-19 causes and links
us-02-multi-replica.feature (replicas boot and serve on one schema)
us-01-install.feature @nfr-port-01, green after every step (amended only in 06-02)
roadmap.deviations_from_distill: DISTILL says un-pend story by story, walking skeleton first. The skeleton needs a page, Generate, Slack save and the reload, so it turns green at 02-04, the earliest step where all four exist. The no-access outline belongs to 02-03, the step that adds its last door, so every row tests something real. The 'generate does not apply' outline belongs to 05-01, because two of its rows need the key file. The key-file reuse scenario belongs to 05-02 because it first needs Generate and the Slack save. 06-02 adds the image-shape @docker-compose scenario and amends @nfr-port-01 (DEVOPS tasks 2 and 3).
prerequisites: Lima VM foundry-test exists (scripts/test-vm-setup.sh). Steps run in order: there is one test VM.
Subprocess (@iis-subprocess) lanes need the debug foundry binary rebuilt and warmed first (cargo build -p foundry-app --bin foundry, then exec it a few times).
roadmap.release_gates: Ships as v0.19.0. No push and no tag without the user's go. Commit after cargo xtask smoke is green; push only after FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1 cargo xtask ci is green in the Lima VM, under timeout. DEVOPS task 7 (CHANGELOG '### Migration notes': 0033 adds tables only, takes seconds, safe for rolling deploys) is done at release time, not as a step.
roadmap.standing_rules: Un-pend (remove @pending) only the owning step's scenarios, and un-pend an outline whole; never re-author DISTILL scenarios (06-02's DEVOPS-assigned scenario is the one exception). Use runtime sqlx::query only. No key, secret, key length or wrapped bytes is ever logged, rendered, audited or Debug-printed. Every time comparison uses the injected Clock. Every instance write takes foundry.instance-integrations, bumps the version and writes its activity row in one transaction. Nothing may depend on a particular hosting environment (AGENTS.md). Mutation kill rate >= 80% on each step's mutation_targets. One local commit per step.
roadmap.lane_preamble: Run every lane under timeout. Rebuild the foundry binary before any @iis-subprocess lane (acceptance uses the prebuilt binary). CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 in the VM.

phases.name: Foundation: settings, the instance store, one boot

steps.name: Instance key settings, legacy aliases and refused starts
steps.description: Read FOUNDRY_INSTANCE_KEY and _PREVIOUS, honouring FOUNDRY_SECRETS_KEY and _PREVIOUS as aliases. An empty value is unset, and the same value under both names counts as the legacy name. Refuse start on a malformed key or on two different values. Add key generation. Read FOUNDRY_DATA_DIR, FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS and the public-URL fallback fact. Covers DEVOPS task 9.
criteria: A malformed key, or the two names set to different non-empty values, refuses start with health.startup.refused naming only the setting or settings, never a value
An empty value under either name is unset; the same value under both counts as the legacy name; a legacy-only instance boots exactly as today
A generated key is 32 random bytes as base64url text that parses back to the same key id

IntegrationSettings::from_lookup over a scenario lookup reports FOUNDRY_DATA_DIR (default /var/lib/foundry), the reload period (default 5000 ms) and whether FOUNDRY_PUBLIC_URL fell back (config.rs table test)
xtask ci's release-build step runs with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_BUILD_OVERRIDE_STRIP=false in its environment, asserted by an xtask unit test on that step's command env (DEVOPS task 9)
scenario_name: Foundry refuses to start on a malformed or conflicting instance key, naming only the setting
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 decision 1; DESIGN D1. A malformed legacy key must still name FOUNDRY_SECRETS_KEY (eip refusal scenarios stay green). TEST PARADIGM: name resolution is pure over a finite domain: (new, legacy) each unset, empty, valid or malformed, plus equal or different. Test the whole domain as an exhaustive table. proptest property: for any 32 bytes, base64url text padded or unpadded parses to the same key id, and generate then parse always succeeds. Subprocess lane: rebuild the binary first.

steps.name: Migration 0033 and the instance integrations store
steps.description: Migration 0033 adds tables only (columns in migration_0033_tables). It is the only migration Deliverable A needs: rewrapped_from_path for 05-03 is included. One store module holds every query on these tables, plus the advisory lock, the version bump, the plan-applying writes for Generate, Move and the Slack save, the reload snapshot, and the replica-state upsert and prune.

migration_0033_tables.integration_secrets_key: id (=1, CHECK, single row), key_id, wrapped_key bytea, wrapped_by_key_id, wrapped_by_source (CHECK operator|file), rewrapped_from_path (nullable), created_by (nullable user ref), created_at (ADR-IIS-001 r2, ADR-IIS-002 r5)
migration_0033_tables.instance_slack_app: id (=1, CHECK), client_id, sealed_client_secret bytea, sealed_signing_secret bytea, saved_by, saved_at (ADR-IIS-003 r1)
migration_0033_tables.integration_config_version: id (=1, CHECK), version bigint, seeded with one row (ADR-IIS-004 r3)
migration_0033_tables.integration_replica_states: replica (PK), applied_version bigint, key_mode, opens_secrets_key boolean, beat_at; no key or key id (ADR-IIS-004 r8)
migration_0033_tables.instance_integration_audit_events: id, actor_id (nullable, ON DELETE SET NULL; NULL = Foundry), action (closed CHECK: secrets_key_generated, credentials_moved, secrets_key_rewrapped, slack_app_saved, secrets_key_replaced, started_over, slack_app_replaced, slack_app_removed), client_id (nullable), count (nullable), created_at (ADR-IIS-005 r1)

criteria: Generate/Move applies a caller-built plan in one transaction under the exclusive lock: create-if-absent key row, every sealed value re-sealed, canary, one activity row, version bump; a store test diffs only those tables
A Move whose re-seal refuses partway (injected failure) leaves integration_secrets_key, every sealed column, key checks, version and activity unchanged (distill upstream-issues item 11)
A second current secrets key cannot be stored; two concurrent Generates store exactly one row

Store test in iis_instance_store.rs: a write committed after the snapshot's version read is absent from that snapshot and its version, so the next snapshot carries it; replica-state upsert and prune use the caller's time
check-arch integrations-instance-tables limits SQL naming the new tables to the store module, with an injected-violation gold test
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 r2 and r5, ADR-IIS-003 r1, ADR-IIS-004 r1, r3, r4 and r8, ADR-IIS-005. The plaintext never reaches the store; keep reseal_credentials' closure shape. instance_slack_app_pending is Deliverable B and goes in B's own migration; this rule still names all six tables. Extend the store's schema probe (PROBE_SQL) to the 0033 tables. Scope the instance-tables rule to production src: the acceptance driver's race count and dump read are DISTILL D5 waivers. TEST PARADIGM: bounded-change store tests, example-based against real Postgres; no proptest.

steps.name: Key mode, credential box and the one shared boot function
steps.description: Add a pure, closed KeyMode decision over settings, held keys and stored rows. Build the credential box: the secrets key is current when Sealed, otherwise the instance key, and every held instance key is a previous key. One shared boot function builds Integrations with mode and probe. main.rs and the acceptance boot, rewire and restart all go through it.
criteria: Mode precedence is NoInstanceKey, then a stored key (Sealed or Unopenable), then Direct or AwaitingSecretsKey; Direct also holds when a stored value is sealed under a held instance key
Legacy direct seals open with no action; external-integration-plugins and integrations-wayfinding stay green
Matrix and Slack offers seal only in Direct or Sealed; the worker runs whenever a held key opens a stored credential
The boot probe proves the canaries of every held key, the stored secrets key's included, and compares key ids of every stored sealed value (connections and saved Slack app)

An in-process restart and a binary restart with the same settings and stored rows report the same secrets verdict, observed through the eip restart scenarios and /metrics probe_failures_total{probe_name="secrets"}
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 r3, r4 and r9; DESIGN D8; brief.md 'Boot and restart'. main.rs and the acceptance boot, rewire and restart_in_process_with_key call the one function; the harness keeps no probe copy. The key source is an injected capability. Until 05-01 there is no file adapter, so with no operator key the mode is NoInstanceKey and the offers read as today's K-18/K-20. SecretsKey and wrapped bytes keep no Debug. TEST PARADIGM: exhaustive table over (operator key, file state, stored key, unwraps, legacy name, direct seals). proptest property over arbitrary sets of stored key ids: sealing is possible iff the mode is Direct or Sealed, and Direct holds whenever no key is stored and some stored id is a held instance key's.

phases.name: Walking skeleton: the page, Generate, the Slack app, every replica

steps.name: Instance integrations page before a secrets key, and the dashboard link
steps.description: Add GET /admin/instance/integrations behind require_instance_admin (uniform 404 for everyone else). Show the I-25 operator line. Show I-3 with Generate, or I-2e0 with Move, per mode. Show the I-9 or I-8 Matrix line. No Slack form without a sealing mode. The instance dashboard gains the I-1 link.
criteria: With an operator key and no secrets key, Priya reads I-25 (operator), I-3 and I-9, is offered Generate and no Slack form
On the legacy setting with nothing saved, Priya reads I-2e0 and I-8 and is offered Move, not Generate
Integrations on /admin/instance/workspaces lands on the instance integrations page
The GET handler only reads
scenario_name: Without a secrets key the page says integrations need one
An instance on the legacy setting with nothing saved yet can move at once, and Matrix is ready
The instance admin dashboard links to the integrations page
steps.implementation_notes: brief.md placement (handlers/instance.rs); DISTILL page seams: buttons are submit controls carrying the copy; activity is [data-instance-integration-activity] li. Buttons may post to doors that answer 404 until 02-02 and 04-01. TEST PARADIGM: the page state, offers included, is a pure function of (mode, app in effect, fallback URL, direct-seal count). Table-test it over every mode. EXEMPT: template wiring is a single-shot render, covered by the scenarios.

steps.name: Generate the secrets key; the sealed page and Slack's addresses
steps.description: POST …/secrets-key builds a pure plan: new key, wrapped under the instance key, canary and activity. The store applies it, and the serving app reloads before it renders I-21. With a key, the page shows I-2, I-5 (manifest, redirect and events URLs from one source) and I-8, plus I-29 when the public URL fell back. Unopenable shows I-26, restore-only.
criteria: Generate answers I-21 and records 'generated the secrets key'; the workspace page offers Connect Matrix and the Matrix route form no longer reads W-2
With a key the page reads I-2, I-5, both URLs and I-8, with no Generate; its manifest and URLs equal GET /workspace/integrations/slack/setup's
With FOUNDRY_PUBLIC_URL unset, I-29 names the fallback URL above the addresses; I-26 (key cannot be unwrapped) offers no Generate, Replace, Start over or Slack form
Tomás (not an instance admin) posting generate gets the uniform not-found page and no secrets key is stored (handler test; the outline un-pends in 02-03)
A Generate post outside AwaitingSecretsKey changes nothing and answers the current page
scenario_name: Generating is recorded
A missing or different instance key is named, never silent
With a secrets key the page shows what to paste into Slack
Unreachable Slack addresses are named before Priya copies them
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 r2 and r5, ADR-IIS-003 r3a, DESIGN D8. The POST is behind require_instance_admin from this step on. Applying a change is synchronous on the serving replica only: after commit it rebuilds through the shared boot and reinstalls locally; the cross-replica poll is 02-04. The Matrix route form's W-2 comes from no_connection.rs following the mode. Manifest equality is also unit-tested on one Integrations. The wrapped value is the key's base64url text. Integrations::slack_events_url is built from EVENTS_PATH, and slack::manifest takes both URLs from Integrations. The POST calls exactly one write use-case and carries _csrf. TEST PARADIGM: proptest property: for any instance key, generate, wrap, unwrap and parse round-trips to the same key id. Table test: the Generate gate over every KeyMode, I-4 included.

steps.name: Save the Slack app, and one access rule for every door
steps.description: POST …/slack seals both secrets into instance_slack_app, in one locked transaction with the version bump and activity. Owns the save and the offers only: the app in effect (environment, else a saved app that opens, else none) decides whether Add to Slack is offered. 03-03 makes events, install and return use the saved app's credentials. Without a sealing mode the POST answers I-3. Every door 404s for anyone but an instance admin.
steps.sizing_review: @sizing-review-needed — accepted: 9 of 11 examples are one outline (uniform 404 on every door) that must un-pend whole in the step adding its last door
criteria: A valid save answers I-10 and I-6 with 'Client secret: set' and 'Signing secret: set', records 'saved the Slack app (<client id>)', and the workspace page offers Add to Slack
A save with no secrets key answers I-3 and stores nothing
No page, GET or POST, shows a key, a secret or a secret's length
Tomás, Lena, Sam, Marco and signed-out visitors get the uniform not-found page on the GET and on every POST, and nothing changes; Priya reaches the page
scenario_name: An instance admin enters the Slack app and Canzan Labs can add Slack at once
Nothing can be saved without a secrets key
Only an instance admin reaches the page or changes anything on it
steps.implementation_notes: See sizing_review (red-classification: the Priya row keeps the others discriminating). ADR-IIS-003 r1, r2 and r7. The save applies on the serving replica synchronously, by a local reinstall after commit; other replicas wait for 02-04's poll. Full shape rules and I-11/I-12 come in 03-02; here a well-formed save succeeds. TEST PARADIGM: the app-in-effect decision over (environment trio set, saved row, both secrets open) is finite. Table-test it exhaustively. EXEMPT: the access guard is shipped require_instance_admin, covered by the outline.

steps.name: Reload on every replica (walking skeleton)
steps.description: Add a reload task per replica, started where main.rs and spawn_app start the app. It polls the config version every FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS, rebuilds through the shared boot function and installs the result. It keeps a held key whose id is unchanged, keeps the last good integrations on failure, and upserts its replica-state row at boot, on apply and every 10 s.
criteria: Generate then Slack save on one replica: within 60 s, with no restart, every replica offers Connect Matrix, then Add to Slack (walking skeleton)
Two simultaneous Generates on two replicas store one key, both answer the resulting state, and a later Slack connection opens on every replica

Reload gold test through the reload task's store capability: a write committed between the version read and the state read is installed by the next tick, and the replica-state row's applied_version reaches it
A failed reload keeps serving the last good integrations and logs integrations.reload.failed; reload never touches the key file
Replica-state rows older than 1 h are pruned by the retention tick, judged by the injected Clock
scenario_name: An instance admin turns on Matrix and then Slack, and every replica offers them without a restart
Two generate requests at the same moment store one key that both replicas use
steps.implementation_notes: @walking_skeleton is green at the end of this step. It depends on 01-01, 01-02, 01-03, 02-01, 02-02 and 02-03. 02-02 and 02-03 already apply on the serving replica synchronously; this step adds the cross-replica poll loop. ADR-IIS-004 r4, r6 and r8. Each replica's AppState runs its own loop; never drive it through MultiReplicaHarness.install_integrations. Besides its own replica-state row, reload writes nothing (store test). TEST PARADIGM: example-based. The reload is an effect shell, and the snapshot gold test is a fixed interleaving. EXEMPT: no pure invariant here beyond 01-03's mode table.

phases.name: The Slack app and the page on existing instances

steps.name: Direct mode with saved credentials and the environment's app
steps.description: The page shows I-2e with Move when stored values are sealed directly under a held instance key, counting them by key id with no stored flag. It shows I-7 when the environment's trio is in effect. Upgrading, or renaming the legacy setting to FOUNDRY_INSTANCE_KEY with the same value, keeps Direct mode and keeps delivering.
criteria: A legacy instance with a direct-sealed connection reads I-2e, is offered Move, reads I-7 with the client ID, and the page holds no key or secret
After a restart with the same settings, a connection sealed with the environment key keeps delivering and the page reads I-2e
After the setting is renamed to FOUNDRY_INSTANCE_KEY with the same value, deliveries continue and the page still reads I-2e
scenario_name: An instance configured before this feature is shown without its secrets
After the upgrade, a connection sealed with the environment key keeps delivering
Renaming the setting to FOUNDRY_INSTANCE_KEY with the same value keeps everything working
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 r3 and r4 (Direct follows direct seals), US-IIS-06 AC 1. The page state table from 02-01 gains the I-2e and I-7 rows. TEST PARADIGM: add those rows to the existing exhaustive table. The direct-seal count is pure over (stored key ids, held instance key ids), so a proptest property checks that it equals the number of stored ids in the held set.

steps.name: Slack app shape check
steps.description: Validate the save as a pure function with no call to Slack. Trim each field. The client ID is digits, a dot and digits; each secret is 32 lowercase hex. A blank field answers I-11 and a malformed one I-12, naming the first failing field in form order. A refusal writes nothing and never takes the lock.
criteria: Each blank field answers I-11 and each malformed field answers I-12, naming that field
The re-rendered form keeps the typed client ID and leaves both secret fields empty
A refused save leaves Slack not set up: no row, no activity, no version bump
scenario_name: A blank or malformed value is refused and nothing is saved
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-003 r3. DELIVER confirms the shapes against recorded Slack values. TEST PARADIGM: a table test over each field's blank, malformed and valid cases, in form order. Three proptest properties: (1) validation of a value is unchanged by surrounding whitespace; (2) any 32 lowercase hex characters are accepted as a secret; (3) any string with a character outside the field's alphabet is refused with I-12.

steps.name: The saved Slack app in effect for events, install and return
steps.description: Owns building Integrations' SlackApp from the app in effect (02-03 decided only the offer): the environment trio wins, otherwise the saved app if both secrets open. Events verify with its signing secret, install uses its client ID, and return exchanges with its client secret. A saved app that does not open shows I-13 and reads W-2 on workspace pages. A save while the environment wins answers I-17.
criteria: Events verify with the saved signing secret, install sends Priya to Slack for the saved client ID, and return connects using the saved client secret
An event signed with any other secret is refused 401
A saved app this Foundry cannot open reads I-13 on the instance page and W-2 on the workspace page
While the environment sets the app, a save answers I-17 and install still uses the environment's client ID
After a restart without the environment's app, the saved app takes over: deliveries continue, the page reads I-6, and events verify
scenario_name: Slack's event check and Add to Slack use the saved app
Add to Slack through the saved app exchanges Slack's code with the saved client secret
An event signed with a secret Foundry was never given is refused
A saved Slack app this Foundry cannot read is not in effect anywhere
While the environment sets the Slack app, a saved app is kept but not used
The saved app takes over when the environment's is removed
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-003 r2 and r6, DESIGN D4. SLACK_API_BASE_URL and SLACK_AUTHORIZE_URL apply to whichever app is in effect. Under I-13, SlackOffer::NotSetUp keeps ADR-IW-001's cause set unchanged. Handlers read the app per request through current(). TEST PARADIGM: extend 02-03's app-in-effect table with the 'saved secrets do not open' rows; the domain is finite, so no proptest. External integration: no new Slack call; ADR-EIP-005's contract-test recommendation stands.

steps.name: Seal fence, the generated-key test seam, and the dump
steps.description: Connection writes (Slack return, Matrix connect) take the instance lock shared and check, in the store transaction, that they sealed under the current sealing key; on a stale key they reload and retry once. Implement the secrets_key_seam reader under integrations-test-seam with a marker, add the Dockerfile's refusal of that marker, and extend integrations-secret-seam.
criteria: Read without the instance key, the database dump yields neither the secrets key, the instance key, the Slack app's secrets nor the Slack token
A second Generate keeps the key: the saved connection still opens and the activity records one generation
A connection write sealed under a stale key is refused in its transaction and retried once after a reload (store test)
check-arch integrations-seal-fence and the extended integrations-secret-seam each fail an injected-violation gold test
The seam is gated on test-support, listed in integrations-test-seam, and its marker is refused by the Dockerfile's grep
scenario_name: A database dump alone opens nothing
A later generate does not replace the key
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-004 r2 (the advisory lock comes before any row lock), ADR-IIS-001 Enforcement, DISTILL D6. DEVOPS task 1 is split: the marker grep lands here, because check-arch integrations-test-seam demands it as soon as the seam is listed. The data directory and VOLUME land in 06-02. The seam takes a PgPool, but SQL on integration_secrets_key may live only in the store module: read the row through a pool-taking store reader. TEST PARADIGM: example-based store and gold tests. EXEMPT: the fence is a transactional effect.

phases.name: US-IIS-06: Move legacy direct seals under a secrets key

steps.name: Move to a secrets key, and Generate and Move withheld under I-4
steps.description: POST …/secrets-key/move runs Generate's use-case: create-if-absent the key, re-seal every instance-key-sealed value (connections and saved app), write the canary and the activity, and bump the version, all in one transaction. It answers I-22 (n = 1 or n ≥ 2), or I-21 when n = 0. Under I-4, Generate and Move are withheld. An unknown key id triggers an immediate, rate-limited reload.
criteria: Move answers I-22 with the count (singular for 1), records 'moved n credentials', and deliveries continue; no connection is marked lost and no admin is emailed
Move with nothing saved answers I-21 and records 'generated the secrets key'
After a Move on one replica, every replica opens the moved credentials within 60 s and lists the next delivery in its route history
When saved credentials open under no held key, the page reads I-4 and offers neither Generate nor Move; a posted Generate or Move answers I-4 and changes nothing
scenario_name: Moving to a secrets key re-seals everything and nobody reconnects
Moving with nothing saved yet just generates the secrets key
Saved credentials no held key opens are named, and generate and move change nothing
After a move on one replica, every replica opens the moved credentials and keeps delivering
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-001 r5, ADR-IIS-004 r5 and r7, DESIGN D2, US-IIS-06 AC 2-3. 01-02's injected-failure store test proves that a refused Move changes nothing. In flight, an open failure stays Transient(secret_unavailable). The unknown-id reload is rate-limited to once per second by the injected Clock. TEST PARADIGM: table tests for the answer words over n in {0, 1, 2, many} and for the withholding gate over every mode with and without I-4. The domain is finite, so no proptest.

phases.name: US-IIS-08: a standalone Foundry makes its own instance key

steps.name: The Foundry-made key file at boot, and its page states
steps.description: key_file.rs is the only code that reads FOUNDRY_DATA_DIR. With no operator key, it reads instance.key or creates it once: temp file O_CREAT|O_EXCL 0600, fsync, link(2), directory fsync, read back. It never overwrites. Wire it, with its probe, into the shared boot. The page shows the I-25 file line, I-27 or I-31.
criteria: Both settings empty: Foundry makes the key file and Priya reads the I-25 file line; both set to one value reads I-2e0
An unwritable data directory reads I-27; the board serves, /readyz is ready, and the workspace page offers neither Slack nor Matrix
An unreadable key file reads I-31, is never changed, and nothing credential-related is offered
Under I-27, I-31 or Direct mode, a posted Generate answers that state and changes nothing
check-arch integrations-key-file-seam fails an injected read of FOUNDRY_DATA_DIR in a handler (gold test)
scenario_name: Empty or matching key settings are read as the operator meant
Without a writable data directory the board serves and the page says why
A key file Foundry cannot read is named, kept, and never replaced
A generate request changes nothing where generating does not apply
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-002 r1, r2, r4 and r6. Earned Trust: wire the adapter, probe it, then use it. Probe faults covered here: read-only directory, short read, corrupt file. Regression guard: eip and wayfinding scenarios with no key setting must never reach the real /var/lib/foundry. Give their in-process and subprocess settings a temp FOUNDRY_DATA_DIR. TEST PARADIGM: example-based fault-injection tests on a temp directory. EXEMPT from proptest: filesystem effects.
lanes: scripts/test-in-lima.sh with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=external-integration-plugins (no-key scenarios, in-process and subprocess)

steps.name: Key file across restarts and servers sharing a directory
steps.description: Harden the adapter under ADR-IIS-002 r2 and r3. Remove leftover instance.key.tmp.* files at boot. Treat link EPERM/ENOTSUP as I-27. Assert a regular 0600 file owned by the running user, warning on wider bits without rewriting. Mint no file when the database holds a secrets key or a direct seal. Read the file at boot only.
criteria: A standalone process makes the key file mode 0600, reads the I-25 file line, and Generate turns on Matrix in one click
Two servers starting together on one directory make exactly one key file; a key generated on the first reads I-2 on the second within 60 s
On restart the key file is unchanged and the saved app is still in effect (I-6, Add to Slack)
A server with a different key file reads I-26 and stays ready; no connection is marked lost and no admin is emailed
Gold tests cover the race, a leftover temp file, link EPERM, the wrong mode, and a stored key with no file
scenario_name: A standalone Foundry makes its own instance key, says what to back up, and turns on Matrix in one click
Servers starting together on one data directory make one key file and share it
The key file is reused, not remade, on restart
A server with a different key file says so and still serves
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IIS-002 r2, r3 and r5 (the self-applying probe). Substrate lies to exercise: an overlayfs fsync no-op, a filesystem without hard links, and a short read during a concurrent write. @iis-subprocess: rebuild and warm the binary first.
